tracks.narration: The S R latch has one forbidden row. What if you turned that forbidden row into the most useful row in digital design?
Here's the JK flip-flop — three inputs J, K, and CLK, two outputs Q and Q-bar. The triangle on the clock input means it samples on the rising edge.
Four operating modes — hold when J equals zero and K equals zero, reset when J is zero and K is one, set when J is one and K is zero, and toggle when both J and K are one.
Hold J and K both at one. Now every rising clock edge flips Q — and Q comes out as a clean square wave at exactly half the clock frequency. That's a one bit binary counter.
Chain N of them and each stage divides by two — N J K flip-flops give you an N bit ripple counter.
